justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Reduces fear of falling and improves balance confidence; fall rate reduction is secondary and modest compared to Otago.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 1-2 day facilitator training; low cost; widely available; easy to implement in community settings.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable in community and geriatric settings; group format limits individual PT caseload application.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Medicare Advantage plans cover in some markets; state fall prevention funding available; standard PT billing applies for clinical delivery.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Primarily sought for community fall prevention programs; limited clinical employer demand.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Group social aspect highly valued; peer modeling of activity reduces fear.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Designed for free/grant-funded community delivery via AAAs; almost no cash-pay model.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Commodity community-health program; zero premium pricing.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Widely available through senior centers; not differentiating.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Coach-trainable group model is leverageable but the revenue model is grant-based.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Low brand awareness among private-pay consumers.
justifications.business.efficiency: Free or very low cost coach training; high efficiency.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Recognized as evidence-based community program but viewed as service/outreach rather than scholarly credential.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful exemplar for community-based falls prevention and IPE coursework.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Solid evidence base from original Boston trial and replications.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Free and fast; high ROI for a community-engagement line on CV.
